question: According to the manual, why might steering be a better option than braking when an obstacle suddenly appears ahead?
choice_a: You can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_b: Steering never requires you to leave your lane
choice_c: Steering automatically engages the antilock braking system
choice_d: Steering causes less wear on the tires than braking
explanation: The manual states that stopping is not always the safest thing to do in an emergency, and you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: What warning does the manual give about making a quick turn in a top-heavy vehicle or a tractor with multiple trailers?
choice_a: It will automatically trigger the ABS malfunction lamp
choice_b: The vehicle may flip over
choice_c: It will void the vehicle's hazardous materials endorsement
choice_d: It cannot be done above 20 mph
explanation: The manual notes that although you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop, top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over when steered quickly.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: If you are forced to return to the road after driving onto the shoulder, what does the manual say you should NOT do?
choice_a: Signal before pulling back onto the road
choice_b: Hold the wheel tightly and turn sharply enough to get back on the road safely
choice_c: Try to edge gradually back onto the road, since your tires might grab unexpectedly and cause you to lose control
choice_d: Check your mirrors before returning to the road
explanation: The manual specifically warns not to try to edge gradually back on the road because the tires might grab unexpectedly and you could lose control; instead, hold the wheel tightly and turn sharply enough to get back on the road safely.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash (Returning to the Road)

question: If you are blocked on both sides and must choose a direction to move, what does the manual say about moving to the right?
choice_a: It should always be avoided because shoulders cannot support a large vehicle's weight
choice_b: It is illegal in most circumstances
choice_c: It only applies when driving a bus, not a truck
choice_d: A move to the right may be best, since it won't force anyone into an opposing traffic lane and a possible head-on collision
explanation: The manual states that if you are blocked on both sides, a move to the right may be best because at least you won't force anyone into an opposing traffic lane and a possible head-on collision.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.1 - Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: How does the manual describe the "controlled braking" method of stopping quickly?
choice_a: Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small
choice_b: Pump the brake pedal rapidly and repeatedly until the vehicle stops
choice_c: Apply the parking brake first, then the service brakes
choice_d: Release the brakes completely the moment the wheels begin to slow
explanation: The manual explains that with controlled braking, you apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements small, and if the wheels lock you release and reapply the brakes as soon as you can.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.2 - How to Stop Quickly and Safely (Controlled Braking)

question: With the "stab braking" method described in the manual, what should you do once you release the brakes and the wheels lock up?
choice_a: Immediately steer sharply to one side
choice_b: Apply the brakes fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling
choice_c: Shift into a higher gear before reapplying the brakes
choice_d: Wait until the vehicle has fully stopped before touching the brakes again
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock, and applying the brakes fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling, noting it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.2 - How to Stop Quickly and Safely (Stab Braking)

question: What does the manual say happens if you jam on the brakes in an emergency by pushing the pedal down as hard as you can?
choice_a: It shortens stopping distance in every situation
choice_b: It automatically activates the parking brake
choice_c: It keeps the wheels locked up and causes a skid, and a skidding vehicle cannot be controlled
choice_d: It has no meaningful effect on vehicle control
explanation: The manual warns that emergency braking does not mean jamming on the brakes, because that will only keep the wheels locked up and cause a skid, and if the wheels are skidding you cannot control the vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.2 - How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: According to the manual, what are the two most common reasons for hydraulic brake failure?
choice_a: Tire blowouts and worn windshield wipers
choice_b: ABS sensor malfunction and worn brake pads
choice_c: Over-acceleration and excessive steering
choice_d: Loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills
explanation: The manual states that most hydraulic brake failures occur for one of two reasons: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade on long hills.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure

question: When the hydraulic brake system won't build up pressure and the pedal feels spongy or goes to the floor, what does the manual say putting the vehicle into a lower gear will do?
choice_a: Help slow the vehicle
choice_b: Restore full hydraulic pressure
choice_c: Automatically deploy the parking brake
choice_d: Disable the ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: The manual advises that when the system won't build up pressure, downshifting into a lower gear will help slow the vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure (Loss of Hydraulic Pressure)

question: Besides downshifting, what two other actions does the manual list for responding to loss of hydraulic pressure?
choice_a: Turning off the engine and coasting to a stop
choice_b: Pumping the brake pedal to generate hydraulic pressure, and using the parking brake, which is separate from the hydraulic system
choice_c: Shifting into neutral and applying the horn continuously
choice_d: Calling for roadside assistance and pulling into the nearest exit
explanation: The manual states that pumping the brake pedal will sometimes generate enough hydraulic pressure to stop the vehicle, and the parking or emergency brake, being separate from the hydraulic system, can also be used to slow the vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure (Loss of Hydraulic Pressure)

question: According to the manual, what is a driver's best hope for stopping a vehicle after the brakes fail on a long downgrade?
choice_a: Shifting into neutral and coasting
choice_b: Turning the engine off
choice_c: An escape ramp
choice_d: Sounding the horn continuously to clear traffic
explanation: The manual states that once brakes have failed on a downgrade, your best hope is an escape ramp, and if there is one, signs will tell you about it.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure (Brake Failure on Downgrades)

question: If no escape ramp is available after brake failure on a downgrade, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Wait as long as possible before leaving the road, since the vehicle will slow on its own
choice_b: Continue downhill in the same gear until the road levels out
choice_c: Steer into the opposing traffic lane where there is more open space
choice_d: Take the least hazardous escape route available, such as an open field or a side road that flattens out or turns uphill, and make the move as soon as you know the brakes don't work
explanation: The manual advises that if no escape ramp is available, take the least hazardous escape route you can, such as an open field or side road, and make the move as soon as you know your brakes don't work, since the longer you wait the harder it will be to stop.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.3 - Brake Failure (Brake Failure on Downgrades)

question: What does the manual say you should assume any time you hear the loud "bang" of a tire blowing?
choice_a: It is your tire, even though it can take a few seconds for your vehicle to react
choice_b: It is always a nearby vehicle, not your own
choice_c: The ABS system has malfunctioned
choice_d: It is safe to keep driving at the same speed
explanation: The manual states that the loud bang of a blowout is easily recognized, and any time you hear a tire blow, you'd be safest to assume it is yours, even though it can take a few seconds for your vehicle to react.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.4 - Tire Failure (Recognize Tire Failure)

question: Why does the manual say you must hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands when a tire fails?
choice_a: A failed front tire can twist the steering wheel out of your hand
choice_b: It engages the antilock braking system
choice_c: It prevents the parking brake from releasing
choice_d: It keeps the tire pressure warning light from activating
explanation: The manual explains that if a front tire fails, it can twist the steering wheel out of your hand, so the only way to prevent this is to keep a firm grip with both hands at all times.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.4 - Tire Failure (Respond to Tire Failure)

question: What does the manual say about using the brakes immediately after a tire fails?
choice_a: Brake as hard as possible immediately to stop before losing control
choice_b: Apply the parking brake immediately instead of the service brakes
choice_c: Stay off the brake, unless you're about to run into something, until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake very gently
choice_d: Pump the brakes rapidly the instant the tire fails
explanation: The manual advises that braking when a tire has failed could cause loss of control, so unless you're about to run into something, you should stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed, then brake gently.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.4 - Tire Failure (Respond to Tire Failure)

question: After you've come to a stop following a suspected tire failure, what does the manual instruct you to do?
choice_a: Continue driving to the next exit before inspecting anything
choice_b: Only inspect the tire that made the loudest noise
choice_c: Wait for roadside assistance to inspect the tires
choice_d: Get out and check all the tires, even if the vehicle seems to be handling all right
explanation: The manual states that after stopping, you should get out and check all the tires even if the vehicle seems to be handling all right, since a failed dual tire may be the only way you know it went by getting out and looking.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.17.4 - Tire Failure (Respond to Tire Failure)

question: According to the manual, what does ABS do to your normal braking capability?
choice_a: It does not decrease or increase your normal braking capability, and only activates when wheels are about to lock up
choice_b: It replaces the normal hydraulic brake system entirely
choice_c: It doubles normal braking capability on wet roads
choice_d: It reduces normal braking capability during light braking
explanation: The manual states that ABS is an addition to your normal brakes; it does not decrease or increase your normal braking capability and only activates when wheels are about to lock up.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18 - Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: How does the manual describe the process by which ABS prevents wheel lockup?
choice_a: The driver manually releases pressure using a dashboard switch
choice_b: Sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and an electronic control unit (ECU) decreases brake pressure to avoid it
choice_c: A mechanical valve in the brake pedal senses road conditions and adjusts pedal resistance
choice_d: The parking brake automatically engages to prevent lockup
explanation: The manual explains that sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and an electronic control unit (ECU) then decreases brake pressure to avoid wheel lockup, adjusting brake pressure to provide maximum braking without danger of lockup.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.1 - How Antilock Braking Systems Work

question: According to the manual, which vehicles are required by the Department of Transportation to have ABS starting with truck tractors built on or after March 1, 1997?
choice_a: Hydraulically braked buses only
choice_b: Motorcoaches with fewer than 16 seats
choice_c: Truck tractors with air brakes
choice_d: Converter dollies manufactured before 1990
explanation: The manual states that the Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.2 - Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Where does the manual say trailers display their yellow ABS malfunction lamp?
choice_a: On the instrument panel next to the speedometer
choice_b: Inside the cargo compartment
choice_c: On the underside of the trailer near the axles
choice_d: On the left side, either on the front or rear corner
explanation: The manual states that trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.3 - How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: On newer ABS-equipped vehicles, what is the malfunction lamp supposed to do at start-up, and what does it mean if it stays on afterward?
choice_a: It comes on for a bulb check and goes out quickly; if it stays on after the check or comes on while driving, you may have lost ABS control
choice_b: It stays on continuously whenever ABS is functioning correctly
choice_c: It never illuminates unless there is a collision
choice_d: It flashes only when the vehicle is in reverse
explanation: The manual explains that on newer vehicles the lamp comes on at start-up for a bulb check and then goes out quickly, and if it stays on after the check or comes on once underway, you may have lost ABS control.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.3 - How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: What benefit does the manual say ABS provides during hard braking, even though it may not always shorten stopping distance?
choice_a: It allows the driver to release the steering wheel safely
choice_b: It should allow you to steer around an obstacle while braking, and avoid skids caused by over braking
choice_c: It automatically reduces vehicle speed to the posted limit
choice_d: It eliminates the need for a fire extinguisher inspection
explanation: The manual states that with ABS you may or may not stop faster, but you should be able to steer around an obstacle while braking and avoid skids caused by over braking.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.4 - How ABS Helps You

question: According to the manual, how should you brake in a vehicle equipped with ABS compared to a vehicle without it?
choice_a: Brake the same way, regardless of whether you have ABS on the bus, tractor, the trailer, or both
choice_b: Apply significantly more brake pressure because ABS compensates automatically
choice_c: Pump the brakes rapidly at all times
choice_d: Use only the parking brake for normal stops
explanation: The manual instructs that you should brake the same way regardless of whether you have ABS on the bus, tractor, trailer, or both, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.6 - Braking with ABS

question: What is the one exception the manual describes to normal ABS braking technique?
choice_a: You should never use the brakes at all if ABS is installed
choice_b: You must disable ABS manually before an emergency stop
choice_c: In a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop
choice_d: You must stab brake even when ABS is functioning normally
explanation: The manual states there is only one exception to the normal braking procedure: if you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, in an emergency stop you can fully apply the brakes.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.6 - Braking with ABS

question: According to the manual's safety reminders, what does ABS NOT allow you to do?
choice_a: Drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully
choice_b: Maintain steering control during hard braking
choice_c: Brake normally under normal conditions
choice_d: Steer around an obstacle while braking
explanation: The manual's safety reminders state that ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.8 - Safety Reminders

question: What does the manual say ABS will NOT compensate for?
choice_a: Wheel lockup during hard braking
choice_b: Bad brakes or poor brake maintenance
choice_c: Over braking on a slippery surface
choice_d: Normal stopping under dry conditions
explanation: The manual's safety reminders explicitly state that ABS won't compensate for bad brakes or poor brake maintenance, and that the best vehicle safety feature is still a safe driver.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.18.8 - Safety Reminders

question: The manual lists four causes of skids. Which of the following is one of them?
choice_a: Under-inflated tires on the steer axle only
choice_b: Driving with an empty cargo tank
choice_c: Over-steering, or turning the wheels more sharply than the vehicle can turn
choice_d: Using the parking brake while parked
explanation: The manual lists over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast as the four causes of skids, defining over-steering as turning the wheels more sharply than the vehicle can turn.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.19 - Skid Control and Recovery

question: According to the manual, what is by far the most common type of skid?
choice_a: A skid in which the front wheels lose traction on a downhill grade
choice_b: A skid caused only by tire blowouts
choice_c: A skid caused by the trailer's brakes locking independently
choice_d: One in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
explanation: The manual states that by far the most common skid is one in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.19.1 - Drive-Wheel Skids

question: In a vehicle towing a trailer, what can a drive-wheel skid cause, according to the manual?
choice_a: The trailer to push the towing vehicle sideways, causing a sudden jackknife
choice_b: The trailer brakes to disengage automatically
choice_c: The ABS malfunction lamp to illuminate permanently
choice_d: The trailer to detach from the fifth wheel
explanation: The manual explains that with vehicles towing trailers, a drive-wheel skid can let the trailer push the towing vehicle sideways, causing a sudden jackknife.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.19.1 - Drive-Wheel Skids

question: What two actions does the manual instruct you to take to correct a drive-wheel braking skid?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake, then release it slowly
choice_b: Stop braking to let the rear wheels roll again, then counter-steer as the vehicle turns back on course
choice_c: Accelerate briefly, then apply the brakes fully
choice_d: Turn the wheel in the direction of the skid and hold it there until stopped
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again, and to counter-steer, since as the vehicle turns back on course it has a tendency to keep turning unless you quickly turn the wheel the other way.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.19.2 - Correcting a Drive-Wheel Braking Skid

question: According to the manual, what mainly causes most front-wheel skids?
choice_a: Over-inflated rear tires
choice_b: Using the speed retarder on a dry road
choice_c: Driving too fast for conditions, along with lack of tread on the front tires or cargo loaded without enough weight on the front axle
choice_d: Riding the clutch on level ground
explanation: The manual states that driving too fast for conditions causes most front-wheel skids, with other causes including lack of tread on the front tires and cargo loaded so not enough weight is on the front axle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.19.3 - Front-Wheel Skids

question: What does the manual list as the three basic steps to take at any accident, if you are not seriously hurt?
choice_a: Move all vehicles to a repair shop, file insurance paperwork, and resume the trip
choice_b: Contact your dispatcher, take photographs, and wait for police
choice_c: Exchange license information, inspect for damage, and clear the scene
choice_d: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured
explanation: The manual states that the basic steps to be taken at any accident are to protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.20 - Accident Procedures

question: What does the manual instruct you to do to protect an accident area if your vehicle is involved?
choice_a: Try to get your vehicle to the side of the road, put on your flashers, and set out reflective triangles
choice_b: Leave the vehicle exactly where it stopped, even if that blocks traffic
choice_c: Turn off your flashers so as not to distract other drivers
choice_d: Wait inside the vehicle with no warning devices displayed
explanation: The manual instructs that if your vehicle is involved in the accident, try to get it to the side of the road, put on your flashers, and set out reflective triangles to warn other traffic, making sure they can be seen in time to avoid the accident.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.20.1 - Protect the Area

question: According to the manual, when should you move a severely injured person at an accident scene?
choice_a: Only if the injured person requests it
choice_b: Only if the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_c: Whenever a qualified person has not yet arrived
choice_d: Immediately, to prevent further injury
explanation: The manual states that you should not move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary, and otherwise should stop heavy bleeding with direct pressure and keep the injured person warm.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.20.3 - Care for the Injured

question: According to the manual, what can cause a vehicle's electrical system to catch fire?
choice_a: Short circuits due to damaged insulation or loose connections
choice_b: Under-inflated tires touching each other
choice_c: Spilled fuel after an accident
choice_d: Poor cargo ventilation
explanation: The manual lists short circuits due to damaged insulation and loose connections as causes of electrical system fires.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.21.1 - Causes of Fire

question: When pulling off the road because of a vehicle fire, what does the manual instruct you to avoid doing?
choice_a: Notifying emergency services of your location
choice_b: Parking in an open area away from buildings or trees
choice_c: Turning off the engine
choice_d: Pulling into a service station
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs, "Don't pull into a service station!" when stopping because of a fire, and instead directs drivers to park in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, or anything that might catch fire.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.21.3 - Fire Fighting

question: For a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, why does the manual say to keep the doors shut, especially with hazardous materials aboard?
choice_a: Opening the doors will supply the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast
choice_b: Opening the doors triggers the vehicle's automatic sprinkler system
choice_c: It is required so bystanders cannot see the cargo
choice_d: It keeps the fire extinguisher's chemical agent from escaping
explanation: The manual warns that opening the van doors on a cargo fire will supply the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast, so the doors should be kept shut, especially for hazardous materials cargo.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.21.3 - Fire Fighting

question: When using a fire extinguisher, where does the manual say you should aim it?
choice_a: Directly up into the flames
choice_b: At the source or base of the fire, staying as far away from the fire as possible
choice_c: At the top of the vehicle regardless of where the fire started
choice_d: Only at the cargo, never at the vehicle body
explanation: The manual instructs that when using the extinguisher, you should stay as far from the fire as possible and aim at the source or base of the fire, not up into the flames.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.21.3 - Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual, why should you avoid using water on an electrical fire or a gasoline fire?
choice_a: Water is never available in sufficient quantity on a commercial vehicle
choice_b: Water is only effective on Class D metal fires
choice_c: Water on an electrical fire can cause shock, and water on a gasoline fire will spread the flames
choice_d: Water evaporates too quickly to be useful on any type of fire
explanation: The manual states that water can be used on wood, paper, or cloth, but should not be used on an electrical fire because it can cause shock, or on a gasoline fire because it will spread the flames.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.21.3 - Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual, what does alcohol impair?
choice_a: Only reaction time, leaving coordination and vision unaffected
choice_b: Only night vision, leaving daytime driving unaffected
choice_c: Only fine motor skills, not judgment
choice_d: Muscle coordination, reaction time, depth perception, and night vision, as well as the parts of the brain that control judgment and inhibition
explanation: The manual states that alcohol impairs muscle coordination, reaction time, depth perception, and night vision, and also affects the parts of the brain that control judgment and inhibition.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.22.1 - Alcohol and Driving

question: According to the manual, why can't black coffee or a cold shower sober up a driver who has been drinking?
choice_a: The liver can only process about one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, a fixed rate that only time can change
choice_b: Coffee and cold water actually increase blood alcohol concentration
choice_c: Alcohol is removed from the body only through the kidneys, not the liver
choice_d: Sobering up depends entirely on body temperature
explanation: The manual explains that the liver can only process about one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is a fixed rate, so only time, not black coffee or a cold shower, will sober a person up.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.22.1 - Alcohol and Driving (How Alcohol Works)

question: According to the manual, what three factors determine a person's Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC)?
choice_a: The type of beverage consumed, the room temperature, and the time of day
choice_b: The amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight
choice_c: The driver's age, driving experience, and vehicle type
choice_d: Whether the drinker ate beforehand, their gender, and the outdoor temperature
explanation: The manual states that BAC is determined by the amount of alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your weight, since a small person doesn't have to drink as much to reach the same BAC.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.22.1 - Alcohol and Driving (What Determines Blood Alcohol Concentration)

question: According to the manual, which function does alcohol affect first as BAC builds up, and why is this dangerous?
choice_a: Vision, which prevents drivers from reading road signs
choice_b: Hearing, which prevents drivers from noticing horns
choice_c: Judgment and self-control, which can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk
choice_d: Balance, which only affects walking, not driving
explanation: The manual explains that the first part of the brain affected by alcohol controls judgment and self-control, and one of the bad things about this is it can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.22.1 - Alcohol and Driving (Alcohol and the Brain)

question: According to the manual, when is possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor permitted while driving?
choice_a: Never, regardless of the doctor's instructions
choice_b: Only if the drug is an over-the-counter cold medicine
choice_c: Only after the driver's shift has ended
choice_d: If the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability
explanation: The manual states that possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor is permitted if the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.22.2 - Other Drugs

question: What does the manual say about using a drug that hides fatigue?
choice_a: It is acceptable for short trips only
choice_b: Don't use any drug that hides fatigue, because the only cure for fatigue is rest
choice_c: It is recommended for long-haul overnight driving
choice_d: It is safe as long as it is combined with caffeine
explanation: The manual states, "Don't use any drug that hides fatigue--the only cure for fatigue is rest," and adds that alcohol can make the effects of other drugs much worse.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.22.2 - Other Drugs

question: According to the manual, what should you do if you become too ill to operate a motor vehicle safely?
choice_a: Continue driving to complete the scheduled route
choice_b: You must not drive, though in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop
choice_c: Pull over and wait exactly one hour before resuming driving
choice_d: Take an over-the-counter medication and continue driving
explanation: The manual states that if you become so ill that you cannot operate a motor vehicle safely, you must not drive, but in case of an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.22.3 - Illness

question: How does the manual define hazardous materials?
choice_a: Any cargo that weighs more than 10,000 pounds
choice_b: Any cargo requiring refrigeration
choice_c: Products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation
choice_d: Only substances classified as radioactive
explanation: The manual defines hazardous materials as products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.23.1 - What Are Hazardous Materials?

question: According to the manual, where must you keep shipping papers related to hazardous materials while driving?
choice_a: In the glove compartment only
choice_b: In the sleeper berth
choice_c: Mailed ahead to the delivery destination
choice_d: In a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle
explanation: The manual states that you must identify hazardous materials shipping papers or keep them on top of other shipping papers, and keep them in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.23.2 - Why Are There Rules?

question: According to the manual, how many identical placards must a placarded vehicle display, and where are they placed?
choice_a: At least four, on the front, rear, and both sides
choice_b: Exactly one, on the rear only
choice_c: Two, on the front and rear only
choice_d: As many as the shipper decides, placed anywhere visible
explanation: The manual states that a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, put on the front, rear, and both sides, and that they must be readable from all four directions.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.23.3 - Lists of Regulated Products

question: According to the manual, what are identification numbers, and what letters typically precede them?
choice_a: Two-digit codes preceded by the letters "HZ"
choice_b: Four-digit codes used by first responders, preceded by the letters "NA" or "UN"
choice_c: Six-digit codes assigned by the driver at the time of loading
choice_d: Codes that appear only on the driver's CDL card
explanation: The manual states that identification numbers are four-digit codes used by first responders to identify hazardous materials, and the number is preceded by the letters "NA" or "UN."
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 2.23.3 - Lists of Regulated Products
